data.name: CasingMismatchTitle
data.value: Casing of symbols and keywords must align with the language definition

data.name: CasingMismatchMessageFormat
data.value: Use '{0}' instead of '{1}' for consistent casing.

data.name: CasingMismatchDescription
data.value: Although incorrect casing is syntactically valid, it is not common practice and reduces readability and recognizability of code.

data.name: CasingMismatchCodeAction
data.value: ALCops: Fix casing

data.name: SemicolonAfterMethodOrTriggerDeclarationTitle
data.value: Procedure or Trigger declaration should not end with semicolon

data.name: SemicolonAfterMethodOrTriggerDeclarationMessageFormat
data.value: The {0} declaration ends with a semicolon. Remove the trailing semicolon from the declaration.

data.name: SemicolonAfterMethodOrTriggerDeclarationDescription
data.value: In AL the semicolon is a statement separator, not a terminator, and procedure or trigger signatures do not require a semicolon at the end. Although the compiler accepts it, enforcing this rule improves consistency and aligns with the coding guidelines used by the community.

data.name: UseParenthesisForFunctionCallTitle
data.value: Function calls should have parenthesis even if they do not have any parameters

data.name: UseParenthesisForFunctionCallMessageFormat
data.value: You must specify open and close parenthesis after '{0}'.

data.name: UseParenthesisForFunctionCallDescription
data.value: Use parenthesis in a function call even if the function does not have any parameters.

data.name: UseParenthesisForFunctionCallCodeAction
data.value: ALCops: Add parenthesis

data.name: UseParenthesisForMethodAssignmentTitle
data.value: Call methods with parenthesis instead of using assignment syntax

data.name: UseParenthesisForMethodAssignmentMessageFormat
data.value: Call method '{0}' using parenthesis instead of assignment syntax.

data.name: UseParenthesisForMethodAssignmentDescription
data.value: A method that takes a single parameter can be invoked using assignment syntax, but this hides that a method is being called and is ambiguous. Call the method using parenthesis instead.

data.name: UseParenthesisForMethodAssignmentCodeAction
data.value: ALCops: Use parenthesis for method call

data.name: PermissionDeclarationOrderTitle
data.value: Permission declarations should be sorted by object type and name

data.name: PermissionDeclarationOrderMessageFormat
data.value: The Permissions property entries are not sorted in the standard order (table/tabledata by name, then codeunit, page, query, report, xmlport).

data.name: PermissionDeclarationOrderDescription
data.value: Permission entries should follow the order produced by the AZ AL Dev Tools "Sort Permissions" command: table and tabledata entries first, interleaved by object name (a table entry precedes the tabledata entry of the same name), followed by codeunit, page, query, report and xmlport entries, each type sorted by object name. Names compare naturally (Item 2 before Item 10), case-insensitively and ignoring spaces. Entries inside #region blocks are sorted within their region; lists that contain other directives (#if, #pragma) or unbalanced #region directives are not checked. A consistent order improves readability and reduces merge conflicts.

data.name: PermissionDeclarationOrderCodeAction
data.value: ALCops: Sort permission declarations

data.name: PermissionValuesShouldBeLowercaseTitle
data.value: Permission values should be lowercase

data.name: PermissionValuesShouldBeLowercaseMessageFormat
data.value: The Permissions property contains uppercase permission values; use lowercase 'r', 'i', 'm', 'd' and 'x' instead.

data.name: PermissionValuesShouldBeLowercaseDescription
data.value: In the Permissions property, the casing of permission values has no runtime effect; both uppercase and lowercase grant the same indirect permission. Uppercase values wrongly suggest that direct permissions are granted, a semantic that only exists in permissionset objects and the InherentPermissions property. Use lowercase values to avoid wrong expectations.

data.name: PermissionValuesShouldBeLowercaseCodeAction
data.value: ALCops: Convert permission values to lowercase

data.name: StatementBlocksSeparatedByBlankLineTitle
data.value: Statement blocks should be separated by a blank line

data.name: StatementBlocksSeparatedByBlankLineMessageFormat
data.value: Statement blocks should be separated. Insert a blank line {0}.

data.name: StatementBlocksSeparatedByBlankLineDescription
data.value: Control-flow statement blocks should be visually separated by blank lines before and after the block, and scope-leaving statements such as Exit and Error() should have a blank line before them.

data.name: AnalyzerExceptionTitle
data.value: Analyzer threw an unhandled exception

data.name: AnalyzerExceptionMessageFormat
data.value: Analyzer '{0}' threw an exception of type '{1}': {2}

data.name: AnalyzerExceptionDescription
data.value: An ALCops analyzer threw an unhandled exception while analyzing this object. This is a defect in the analyzer, not in the analyzed code. The diagnostic is reported at the object or line being analyzed (instead of the generic AD0001 on app.json) so the culprit can be located. Please report it to the ALCops maintainers with the object name and exception details.
